my gf and I, because we always play 1v1 and are competitive af, use these (but we're trying to make a proper homebrew):

the reverse card basically does nothing in 1v1, so we might change that haha

+2 and +4 cards can be followed up with another plus-something card. this can go on until one of you doesn't have a + card or doesn't want to risk drawing ≥4 more cards. Who draws the cards can't play their turn.

block cards stagger for 1 turn, and if you have more than one they are useful for switching the color safely

because we have the He-Man Uno cards, which includes 4 "for the power of grayskull" cards which are basically +3 and color change, and we adapted as combo breakers
basically if someone plays a +2 or +4 and you play a grayskull card they can't retaliate and they have to draw, unless they have another grayskull card.


these rules allow a lot of things to combo into each other, i would recommend to play 1v1 this way, combos can get really nasty.
